Quantify and report the uncertainty of isoform-level results

Source: R/uncertainty.R
uncertainty.Rd

An isoform-level result is only as good as the quantification behind it. Reads that map to several isoforms of a gene can be shared out between them in more than one way, so the estimate of each isoform carries an inferential uncertainty that is unrelated to biological variability. Salmon measures it by drawing replicates from the posterior (Gibbs sampling, --numGibbsSamples) and by writing the equivalence classes (--dumpEq). These functions turn that information into columns that can be filtered on and reported.

Every isoform gets four kinds of evidence:

  • Quantification uncertainty: the inferential relative variance (mean_inf_rv, Zhu et al. 2019, as in fishpond), the variance of the replicates in excess of what counting noise alone would give, relative to the expression. Isoforms with a high value are not well determined by the reads. uncertain flags mean_inf_rv >= inf_rv_cutoff.

  • Identifiability: the correlation between the replicates of isoforms of the same gene. A strong negative correlation means the reads cannot tell the two isoforms apart and every read taken from one is given to the other. Pairs at or below cor_cutoff are ambiguous and are joined into ambiguity_groups that can be tested as one feature.

  • Read support: the share of the fragments of an isoform that map to it alone (unique_fraction, from the equivalence classes).

  • Stability of the fold-change: the contrast between two groups is repeated on every replicate. lfc_lo/lfc_hi is the 95% interval of the log2 fold-change over replicates, sign_agreement the share of replicates that agree on its direction and frac_draws_sig the share in which the isoform is called differentially expressed.

de_confidence() combines the last three into one class per isoform: high when the fold-change is stable (sign_agreement >= min_agreement), the isoform is not uncertain and has no ambiguous sibling; moderate when exactly one of these fails; low when two or more fail. The class says how far a call on the isoform can be trusted, so read it for the isoforms flagged by the primary test (n_det_sig, confident_de): an isoform without a real change is moderate or low simply because its fold-change is not stable.

  • add_uncertainty(x, paths) reads the replicates, equivalence classes and run metadata from the Salmon output directories paths (named by sample ID, in any order), computes the tables below and stores them in the object, so that they are written by write_isoformic(). When group is given it also stores the fold-change stability of that contrast.

  • tx_uncertainty(x): per-transcript table, for the transcripts whose draws are in the object (the expressed ones).

  • isoform_ambiguity(x): per-pair table of replicate correlations.

  • de_confidence(x, group): per-feature table of fold-change stability and confidence class; with collapse_groups = TRUE, ambiguous isoforms are summed into one feature before testing.

  • uncertainty_report(x): a list of summary tables for a methods or results section.

  • uncertainty_methods(x): a ready-to-edit paragraph that states the settings used.

The replicates themselves are kept in memory only (in metadata(x)$inf_reps) and are not written by write_isoformic(); the tables derived from them are. Draws are kept for the transcripts with an estimated mean count of at least min_count; the others are treated as unexpressed.

Usage

add_uncertainty(
  self,
  paths = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  n_draws = NULL,
  min_count = 1,
  inf_rv_cutoff = 0.5,
  cor_cutoff = -0.5,
  min_agreement = 0.95,
  equivalence = TRUE,
  run_qc = TRUE,
  keep_draws = TRUE,
  collapse_groups = FALSE,
  groups = NULL,
  ...
)

tx_uncertainty(self, gene_name = NULL, ...)

isoform_ambiguity(self, gene_name = NULL, ambiguous_only = FALSE, ...)

de_confidence(
  self,
  group = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  collapse_groups = FALSE,
  gene_name = NULL,
  pseudocount = 5,
  inf_rv_cutoff = NULL,
  min_agreement = NULL,
  ...
)

uncertainty_report(self, ...)

uncertainty_methods(self, ...)

Arguments

self

An IsoformicExperiment.

paths

Salmon output directories (see read_inferential_replicates()), named by sample ID. NULL uses the replicates already stored in the object.

group

Name of a col_data() column with the sample groups.

levels

The two group levels to contrast, reference first. NULL uses the levels of group, which must then be exactly two.

n_draws

Number of replicates to read; NULL reads all of them.

min_count

Minimum mean estimated count for a transcript to be assessed.

inf_rv_cutoff

Inferential relative variance from which an isoform is called uncertain. NULL uses the value the tables were computed with.

cor_cutoff

Mean replicate correlation at or below which two isoforms of a gene are called ambiguous. NULL uses the stored value.

min_agreement

Share of replicates that must agree on the direction of a fold-change for it to be called stable. NULL uses the stored value.

equivalence

Logical, read the equivalence classes when present, or the table returned by equivalence_support(), to attach read support when the draws are supplied without paths.

run_qc

Logical, add the Salmon run metadata (see salmon_run_qc()) to col_data().

keep_draws

Logical, keep the replicates in the object (needed to recompute the tables and for productive_fraction() uncertainty).

collapse_groups

Logical, sum ambiguous isoforms into one feature before testing the contrast.

groups

External groups of transcripts that the reads cannot tell apart, replacing the groups built from the correlation of the replicates: a table with transcript_id and group_id, or the path to Terminus output (see read_terminus_groups()), or the cut of TreeTerminus trees (see cut_transcript_trees()). The confidence classes and collapse_groups then follow these groups; the pairs of isoform_ambiguity() keep describing the correlation.

...

Unused.

gene_name

Optional gene names or IDs to keep.

ambiguous_only

Logical, isoform_ambiguity() returns only the ambiguous pairs.

pseudocount

Pseudocount of the log2 fold-change (5, as in swish).

Value

  • add_uncertainty(): the object with dea$uncertainty, dea$ambiguity and, when group is given, dea$confidence filled in.

  • tx_uncertainty(): a tibble with transcript_id, gene_id, names and type, mean_count, mean_inf_rv, max_inf_rv, mean_inf_cv, uncertain, min_sibling_cor, n_ambiguous_partners, ambiguity_group and, when equivalence classes were read, n_classes, n_unique_fragments and unique_fraction.

  • isoform_ambiguity(): a tibble of isoform pairs of the same gene with mean_cor, min_cor, n_samples and ambiguous.

  • de_confidence(): a tibble with one row per feature: feature_id, feature_type ("transcript" or "group"), gene and transcript names, the interval and stability of the fold-change, mean_inf_rv, ambiguous, confidence (an ordered factor), reason, the existing differential expression result (det_log2FC, det_qvalue, n_det_sig) and confident_de, which is TRUE when a significant isoform has high confidence.

  • uncertainty_report(): a list with settings, run, transcripts (by transcript type), genes, de and switches tibbles.

  • uncertainty_methods(): a character string.

Details

The thresholds are heuristics, not universal constants: inf_rv_cutoff (0.5), cor_cutoff (-0.5) and min_agreement (0.95) are conservative starting points. With 30 draws, sampling noise alone puts the inferential relative variance of a well-determined, highly expressed transcript near 0.1, so cutoffs much below 0.5 flag noise; poorly determined isoforms typically reach values of several units. Report the numbers next to the classes, and rerun with other cutoffs if the data call for it. The replicates measure the uncertainty of the quantification only; they do not replace biological replicates and cannot make a noisy contrast significant.

Fold-changes are computed on counts scaled to a common library size, as log2(mean_b + pseudocount) - log2(mean_a + pseudocount) with a pseudocount of 5 (the swish convention), and the per-replicate test is a Welch t-test on the log scale with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across features. This is a screening statistic for stability, not a replacement for the primary test (swish, DESeq2, ...), whose results are shown next to it. When the sample table (col_data) has a library_size column, with the total estimated count of the full quantification, it is used for the scaling. Set it when the object holds only a subset of the transcripts, so that the subset does not change the scaling.

References

Zhu, A., Srivastava, A., Ibrahim, J.G., Patro, R., Love, M.I. (2019). Nonparametric expression analysis using inferential replicate counts. Nucleic Acids Research 47(18), e105.

See also

read_inferential_replicates(), plot_de_confidence(), isoform_switches()

Examples

quant_dirs <- list.files(
  system.file("extdata", "mini_quants", package = "isoformic"),
  full.names = TRUE
)
names(quant_dirs) <- sub("_quant$", "", basename(quant_dirs))
annot <- system.file("extdata", "mini_annotation", package = "isoformic")
col_data <- data.frame(
  sample_id = names(quant_dirs),
  condition = rep(c("control", "treatment"), each = 3)
)
iso <- read_salmon(quant_dirs, annot_path = annot, col_data = col_data)
#> Warning: NAs introduced by coercion
#> Warning: NAs introduced by coercion
#> Warning: NAs introduced by coercion

# With your own data, `read_salmon(dirs, annot, inferential = TRUE)` or
# `add_uncertainty(iso, paths = dirs)` read the replicates that
# `salmon quant --numGibbsSamples 30` wrote; here bundled draws are used
draws <- as_inferential_replicates(read_parquet(
  system.file("extdata", "mini_draws.parquet", package = "isoformic")
))
iso@metadata$inf_reps <- draws
iso <- add_uncertainty(iso, group = "condition")
head(tx_uncertainty(iso))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 14

#> #   mean_inf_cv <dbl>, uncertain <lgl>, min_sibling_cor <dbl>,

isoform_ambiguity(iso, ambiguous_only = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 10

head(de_confidence(iso))
